key_insight: HealthClaw is a self-evolving health AI agent that separates shared safety/medical rules from private longitudinal memory so it can adapt support as a person’s health changes over time.
clinical_relevance: This could help future digital health tools deliver more personalized, privacy-aware support across repeated encounters, but it is not yet proven in real clinical use.
method: Uses a memory architecture with shared safety rules plus private longitudinal memory.
Stores profile facts, reusable procedures, and episodic traces separately.
Runs an induction step after each episode to decide what to update, keep episodic, or exclude.
evidence_signal: In synthetic and biomedical offline evaluations, HealthClaw improved longitudinal answer accuracy to 45.7% from 0.2% with current-query prompting, reduced prompt context exposure by 71.7%, and showed a mean 27.0-point gain across nine biomedical tasks.
watch_item: Results are based on offline synthetic and benchmark tasks, so prospective clinical validation is still needed before real-world deployment.
paper_title: A Self-Evolving Agent for Longitudinal Personal Health Management
